### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7e6e8a464799af6271410ec6b4b3e119716e2f3a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `878b64eed05f134b2b1395196a54af2159bbf599` — the merge of head `157212e35382baefae19cf88da5c942d587fcaf5` into base `7e6e8a464799af6271410ec6b4b3e119716e2f3a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 878b64eed05f134b2b1395196a54af2159bbf599 && git checkout 878b64eed05f134b2b1395196a54af2159bbf599
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7e6e8a464799af6271410ec6b4b3e119716e2f3a 157212e35382baefae19cf88da5c942d587fcaf5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7e6e8a464799af6271410ec6b4b3e119716e2f3a && git merge --no-ff 157212e35382baefae19cf88da5c942d587fcaf5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7e6e8a464799af6271410ec6b4b3e119716e2f3a
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `157212e35382baefae19cf88da5c942d587fcaf5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/ui/action-params.zod.ts (`validateActionParams`, `ResolvedActionParam`), packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (`resolveDeclaredActionParams`, the caller that keys a field-backed param), packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts (`create_user`, the one repeated name in the tree) and its `sys-user-create-user-email-required.test.ts`, packages/spec/src/ui/action-params.test.ts (the #28280 pins), objectui `packages/fields/src/resolveActionParams.ts` (`paramName`, the dialog's key). The remaining paths (`.changeset/28732-action-params-same-name-rule.md`, the four regenerated `content/docs/references/**/*.mdx`) are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; they were read to judge the `hits` file, not reviewed.

Inputs read: card #28732 body and its three comments (triage `6560352773`, claim `6560638974`, os-dev-report `6561191307`); PR #28752 body and file list (6 files); the net diff `8bceb6a2…157212e3` (+16/−6, 4 commits); the check-runs on `157212e3` (see ① / ③).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set: unchanged — right.** The only source hunk replaces the string inside `.describe()` on `ActionSchema.params` (`action.zod.ts:1431`). No key, refinement, transform or error map moves; `z.array(ActionParamSchema).optional()` is the same schema before and after. A repeated name still parses silently, exactly as the card asked (no new gate, 「新增门禁默认否」). The accept-set the dev names in the PR body (nothing accepted or refused differently) matches the tree.
- **Public surface: the description text only — right.** `.describe()` ships three ways, each the same sentence: `dist` (the zod schema), `json-schema/` (gen:schema, build output, untracked) and the generated references. All four `.mdx` rows carrying the `params` member (`Action` and `InlineAction` in `ui/action.mdx`, `ActionButtonProps` in `ui/component.mdx`, the embedded action tables in `data/object.mdx` and `kernel/metadata-plugin.mdx`) carry the new sentence and no stale copy of the old one remains (`git grep` at head: 5 files, every occurrence of the first sentence is followed by the new one). `check:generated` / `check:docs` on the head are the gate for that; their conclusions are in ③.
- **Shared description reaches `InlineAction` / `ActionButtonProps` — right, with one reading noted in ④.** The description lives on the one `actionObject()` factory, so the sentence is also served on the inline page-button form. That is where the first sentence already lived; the dev did not fork it, correctly.
- **Wording widened from the order's literal (`name`) to `name` or `field` — right.** `resolveDeclaredActionParams` (runtime `action-execution.ts:2801`) keys every declaration by `p?.name ?? fieldRef`, `ActionParamSchema.name`'s own docblock says "Defaults to `field` when `field` is set", the `ai.paramHints` refine keys by `p.name ?? p.field` (`action.zod.ts:2218`) and objectui's `paramName` reads `param.name ?? param.field`. The one repeated name in the tree, `sys_user.create_user`'s `email`, is declared twice through `field` (`sys-user.object.ts:331-332`), so a sentence naming only `name` would not have covered the case that motivated the rule.
- **`Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` — right.** No authored key, value or default changes; nothing stored moves. `check:authorable-surface` and `check:api-surface` are not touched by `.describe()` text.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` **patch** — matches. The change is description text inside a shipped schema (`dist`, `json-schema/`, `src/**/*.zod.ts` are all in spec's `files[]`), so a changeset is owed and patch is the floor and the ceiling: no type, no accepted value, no refusal moves. The changeset carries `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, in agreement with the PR body and with the diff. `Check Changeset` on the head: success.

Clause-②: no — judged from the tree, not from the PR body: the authoring input type of `ActionSchema` (what `defineAction` publishes) is unchanged, and the only moved bytes are inside a string literal passed to `.describe()`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation 1 — "Description names `name` or `field` (the order's sentence named the name only)."** Answered: right, see ①. The widening is not a vocabulary change; it names the two spellings the resolver already folds into one request key.
- **Deviation 2 — "`test:repo` not run locally; CI Test Core runs it."** Answered by the head's check-runs, which are the gate verdicts for this review: 65 check-runs on `157212e3`, all completed, 57 success and 8 skipped (opt-in / matrix-template / schedule-gate rows), 0 failure, 0 cancelled. Among the successes: Test Core (1/8–8/8), Test UI (1/16–16/16), Build Core, Build Docs, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped (×3), Type Check · workspace / source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Type Check UI, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes. The locally NOT-MEASURED `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` rides the Lint gate jobs, which are green.
- **`open_questions: []`.** The card offered one conditional open question: a parse-time refusal of drifting shapes (same name, different `type`), to be raised only with a real case. The dev raised none. Agreed on the tree: `create_user`'s two `email` declarations read the same field and declare no `type`, so their resolved shape cannot differ; `action-params.test.ts:51-58` pins FIRST-wins over a deliberately drifting pair as the contract, so the validator's behaviour on drift is already a decided answer, not an unknown. No producer in the tree writes a drifting pair. Not escalated.
- **`out_of_scope_findings: []`.** Nothing to add.
- **Local-runs: none.** Nothing built, run or re-run here; `node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template` was read for the record's shape only.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts`** — judged against the ruling it implements (card #28732 "Wanted": the `params` description says a name may repeat only for per-gate variants of one input, `required` holds only when every declaration requires it, the first declaration's type wins; no new gate) and against its first consumer, the validator the sentence describes (`validateActionParams`, `action-params.zod.ts:185-230`) as fed by `resolveDeclaredActionParams` on the one real instance (`sys_user.create_user`).

Each clause of the sentence, read against the code:

1. *"A param name (its `name`, or the `field` a field-backed param reads)"* — holds. The resolver's key is `p?.name ?? fieldRef`; `ResolvedActionParam.name` is "inline `name`, or the resolved field name". The parenthetical reads as "`name`, else `field`", which is the resolver's precedence (a field-backed param that also sets `name` is keyed by `name`), so it does not invert it.
2. *"may repeat only for per-gate variants of ONE input (declarations that differ in `visible` / `requiresFeature`, e.g. one optional and one required)"* — holds as the card's norm, unenforced by design. `requiresFeature` is lowered into `visible` at parse time (`lowerRequiresFeature`, `action.zod.ts:588`; its describe says so), so naming both spellings is the author-side vocabulary, not two mechanisms. The example is the tree's only instance (`sys-user.object.ts:331-332`: `required: false, requiresFeature: 'phoneNumber'` then `required: true, visible: 'has(features.phoneNumber) && features.phoneNumber != true'`).
3. *"the params check treats the name as `required` only when EVERY declaration of it requires it"* — holds: `declared.set(p.name, first ? { ...first, required: Boolean(first.required && p.required) } : p)` (`action-params.zod.ts:206-207`); pinned by `action-params.test.ts:36-48` in both orders.
4. *"judges its value by the FIRST declaration's shape (`type`, `multiple`, `options`)"* — holds: the spread keeps the first declaration's `type`/`multiple`/`options` and only `required` is folded; `valueSchemaFor({ type, multiple, options })` at `:221` is the whole shape the check reads, and `ResolvedActionParam` carries no other shape key, so the three-word list is complete, not a sample. Pinned by `action-params.test.ts:51-58`.
5. *"so keep that shape identical across them"* — the right advisory for a rule the schema deliberately does not enforce: the console (`filterVisibleParams`, per the `create_user` test header) renders whichever declaration's gate says yes, so a second declaration with a different `type` would be collected by the dialog under its own shape and then judged by the first's; the sentence tells the author exactly which side wins.

Attempts to break it:
- *Does the sentence promise an enforcement that does not exist?* No. It says "may repeat only…" (the norm) and "the params check treats… judges…" (what runs). It never says the schema refuses anything, and nothing in `ActionSchema` was given a refusal.
- *Does it misstate the key for a field-backed param that also sets `name`?* No (clause 1 above).
- *Does it reach surfaces where the params check does not run?* The sentence is also served on `InlineAction` / `ActionButtonProps` (same factory). On a page button of `type:'api'` whose `target` is a foreign endpoint the ADR-0104 D2 check is not the thing judging the body. The first sentence of the description has always been shared the same way, the rule is still the platform's own and the advisory ("keep that shape identical") is harmless there. Noted, not a finding.
- *Does the generated reference drift from the source?* No: five rows across four `.mdx` files, all byte-identical to the `.describe()` text (one `\'` unescaped by the generator), and no stale copy remains.

Findings:
- **should-fix (minor):** "the params check" is unnamed. Every other description on this schema that cites an enforcer names it (e.g. "refused by `@objectstack/lint` (`action-dispatch-contract-mismatch`)"). Naming the check — `validateActionParams` (ADR-0104 D2), applied on the platform action route — would let an author or an AI reading the generated reference find the behaviour it describes, and would also tell an inline-`api`-button author that the rule is the platform's dispatch check, not their foreign target's. Text only; can follow in a later description PR or at the seat's discretion.
- No must-fix. The sentence states the rule the validator applies, with the same precedence and the same shape list, and the one repeated name in the tree is exactly the case it describes.

> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
